newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Upto 50 percent of the murders committed in Bangladesh are due to husbands' violence against wives, says a UN report.
Some 803 Bangladeshi workers, deported by Saudi Arabia for illegal stay, is due to arrive in Chittagong on Thursday.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina will visit Japan from July 1 in quest of Japanese investment.
Nearly 30 percent of the outdoor patients in hospitals and health centres suffer from sexually transmitted diseases, a health seminar was told on Wednesday.
Tribal refugee leaders and Indian officials from Tripura state are due to arrive in Khagrachari hill district on Thursday to monitor rehabilitation of the repatriated refugees.
An integared rural development project will be implemented in 17 coastal districts within a year to ensure safty of life and property of the people living in the cyclone-prone coastal belt.
Shrimp sector suffered losses to the tune of 3.3 billion taka in last week's cyclone and tidal surge, shrimp farm owners association said.
Bangladesh's literacy rate would be raised to 90 percent in next 10 years from the existing 40 percent, Education Minister A S H K Sadeque said. REUTER
